models.name: economic_board_citizens
models.description: Main table storing citizen account information including email, password hash, display name, bio, and account status (active/banned/deleted).

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for authentication. Must be verified before account activation.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: bcrypt hash of the user's password for secure authentication.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Publicly visible name for profile presentation. Must be unique among all citizens.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional personal bio text displayed on user profile. Limited to 500 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was created. Always set to current server time in Asia/Seoul timezone.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was last updated. Automatically updated on any profile change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the account was deleted (soft delete). Null indicates active account.

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the account was banned. Null indicates account is not banned.

plainFields.name: is_verified
plainFields.description: Boolean flag indicating whether email verification has been completed. Defaults to false on account creation.

plainFields.name: is_banned
plainFields.description: Boolean flag indicating whether account is currently banned. Maintained for query performance and synchronization with banned_at timestamp.

models.name: economic_board_citizen_sessions
models.description:
Stores JWT access and refresh tokens for citizen sessions, with creation and expiration timestamps for session management.

This is a session table that maintains the authentication state of citizens. Each record represents a single login session and contains connection metadata to track where and when users logged in. Session tables only maintain connection context and temporal information - they do not store user profile data or authentication credentials.

Session records are created during authentication and invalidated during logout or expiration. The expired_at field ensures sessions have limited lifetimes for security, while the created_at field allows auditing of login patterns.

This table is referenced exclusively by the authentication flow and is never directly accessed by business logic or frontend interfaces. Instead, users interact with the system using JWT tokens obtained from these sessions.

@link economic_board_citizens.id

foreignFields.name: economic_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who owns this session. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: The IP address from which the session was initiated. Used for security auditing and geolocation purposes.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL path the user was visiting when initiating the session. Tracks user entry point into the system.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The previous web page that linked to the authentication endpoint. Used for traffic analysis and security detection.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created. This field is mandatory for all session records to enable auditing of login events.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires. Sessions have a limited lifetime for security. When expired_at is reached, the session is no longer valid and the user must re-authenticate.

models.name: economic_board_citizen_email_verifications
models.description:
Holds email verification tokens for citizen registration, enabling secure confirmation of email ownership before account activation. This table stores temporary verification tokens that citizens use to confirm their email addresses during registration. Each token has a limited lifespan enforced by an expiration timestamp, ensuring tokens cannot be used indefinitely. Once verified, the token is invalidated and no longer usable. This table maintains the security of the registration process by preventing unauthorized email address changes.

This table is exclusively used for citizen verification and is not shared with administrators or super administrators. Foreign key relationships with the citizen actor (economic_board_citizens) are managed by the Authorization Agent and not modeled in this schema since the actor table is in a separate component.

plainFields.name: citizen_id
plainFields.description: The citizen account ID that this verification token belongs to. This references the citizen actor account that is undergoing email verification.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: The unique verification token generated for email confirmation. This token is sent to the user's email address and must be presented to complete registration.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this verification token expires and becomes invalid. Tokens must be used before this time to complete email verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this verification token was created.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this token was successfully used to verify the email address. Null if the token has not been used yet.

models.name: economic_board_citizen_password_resets
models.description:
Stores password reset tokens for citizens with expiration timestamps to enable secure password recovery workflows. Each record represents a single password reset request initiated by a citizen. The token is a unique, random string that must be presented to reset the password. The expires_at field ensures tokens are temporary and invalid after a set period (e.g., 1 hour). When used, the record is deleted to prevent replay attacks. This table is only referenced by the authentication service and has no direct user-facing interface. Foreign key to economic_board_citizens.id. The table follows the session stance because it tracks a specific authentication workflow tied to the citizen actor.

Related entities: 
- {@link economic_board_citizens} - citizen account owning this reset request
- {@link economic_board_citizen_sessions} - other authentication session records

foreignFields.name: economic_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen account that requested this password reset. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique, random token string generated for this password reset request. Must be URL-safe and cryptographically random. Used in the reset link sent via email.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token expires. After this time, the token becomes invalid and cannot be used to reset the password. Typically set to 1 hour after created_at.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset request was created.

models.name: economic_board_administrators
models.description: Main table storing administrator account information including email, password hash, display name, bio, and account status (active/banned/deleted). This table serves as the canonical identity record for administrators, with its own authentication flow and session tracking managed separately in economic_board_administrator_sessions. Administrators use this identity to perform elevated operations including section management and banning users. All administrators must be properly authenticated before accessing administrative features.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and communication. Must be a valid business email address.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password using bcrypt algorithm with cost factor of 12. Never stored in plain text. Used for secure authentication verification.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public-facing identifier displayed to other users on articles and comments. Must be unique across all user types. Maximum 50 characters.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Short biography text describing the administrator's background or areas of expertise. Maximum 500 characters.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account status indicating whether the administrator is active, banned, or deleted. Valid values: 'active', 'banned', 'deleted'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created. Always set to server time (Asia/Seoul) at account creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was last updated. Automatically updated on any profile modification.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was logically deleted. NULL if account is still active. Used for soft deletion to preserve audit trail.

models.name: economic_board_administrator_sessions
models.description: Stores JWT access and refresh tokens for administrator sessions, with creation and expiration timestamps for session management. Each session is tied to exactly one administrator via administrator_id, maintains connection metadata (IP address, referrer, href), and enforces session lifecycle through generated and expired timestamps. This table follows the session stance pattern: append-only audit trail of login events, managed through authentication flows and not direct user CRUD operations. Every record represents a single login event, with no duplicate sessions for any administrator at any given time. A session becomes invalid when expired_at is reached or when the administrator logs out, changes password, or is banned.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator this session belongs to. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the administrator logged in. Captured at time of session creation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The full URL path and query string that the administrator was accessing when logging in.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The URL that referred the administrator to the login page. Optional field, may be null if no referrer information is available.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created and the administrator successfully logged in. Always set to the server's current time (Asia/Seoul timezone) at login.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires and becomes invalid. Always set to created_at + 14 days (336 hours) for refresh token expiration, or +20 minutes (1200 seconds) for access token expiration. Used to enforce session lifetime.

models.name: economic_board_administrator_email_verifications
models.description: Holds email verification tokens for administrator registration, enabling secure confirmation of email ownership before account activation. Each verification token is single-use and expires after 7 days. This table enables the administrator registration workflow by confirming that the email address provided during signup belongs to the user. The token is sent via email and must be presented to complete registration. Once the token is verified, the record is marked as deleted_at but retained for audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator account this verification belongs to. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token generated for the email confirmation link. Must be URL-safe and generated with cryptographically secure randomization. Used once and invalidated upon successful verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the email verification record was created. Set to the exact time of registration request.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token expires. Must be set to 7 days after created_at for security.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification record was marked as deleted (after successful verification). Used for soft deletion and audit trail. NULL means the token is still active and unverified.

models.name: economic_board_administrator_password_resets
models.description: Stores password reset tokens for administrators with expiration timestamps to enable secure password recovery workflows. Each token is unique, single-use, and expires after 24 hours. This table is referenced by the authentication service when administrators request password reset via email. When a reset token is used, it is immediately invalidated and removed from this table. The table is append-only and never updated once created.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator account this reset request belongs to. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: The unique, cryptographically secure password reset token generated for the administrator. This token must be URL-safe and unique across the system.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the reset token expires. Tokens are valid for 24 hours from creation and are automatically invalidated after this time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the password reset request was created. Used for auditing and calculating token validity duration.

models.name: economic_board_super_administrators
models.description: Main table storing superAdministrator account information including email, password hash, display name, bio, and account status (active/banned/deleted). This table serves as the canonical identity record for super administrators who have elevated permissions to manage admin requests, promote/demote other administrators, and perform all administrative actions without restriction. Super administrators are distinct actor entities with their own authentication flows and cannot be demoted by regular administrators.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for login and authentication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hashed password for secure authentication. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown on user profiles and content interactions.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biography or personal statement about the super administrator.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account status: 'active', 'banned', or 'deleted'. Determines whether the user can authenticate.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the super administrator's account information.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the account was marked as deleted (soft delete). Nullable - indicates active account if null.

models.name: economic_board_super_administrator_sessions
models.description:
Stores JWT access and refresh tokens for superAdministrator sessions, with creation and expiration timestamps for session management.

This table is a session tracking entity for the superAdministrator actor type. Each record represents a single authenticated session started by a superAdministrator. The table contains session metadata including IP address, referrer, and href, which are essential for security auditing and session monitoring. This table does not store actual token values but captures the context of the login session. When a superAdministrator logs in, a new record is created; when they log out or the session expires, the record remains for audit purposes but becomes inactive. This structure enables tracking of login patterns, geographic locations, and potential security incidents.

{@link economic_board_super_administrators.id} references the superAdministrator who initiated the session.

Note: This table follows the strict session pattern defined in the AutoBE architecture and must NOT contain any additional fields beyond those specified in the core design principles.

foreignFields.name: super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the superAdministrator who initiated this session. {@link economic_board_super_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: The IP address from which the session was initiated. Used for security monitoring and geolocation tracking.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL of the page the superAdministrator was on when initiating the session. Used for navigation context and potential security analysis.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL indicating the source from which the superAdministrator navigated to the platform. Used for traffic analysis and security auditing.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when the session was created. This field is required for session duration calculation and security audit trails.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when the session will expire. This field is required for automatic session cleanup and to enforce session timeouts as a security practice.

models.name: economic_board_super_administrator_email_verifications
models.description:
Holds verification tokens for superAdministrator registration, enabling secure confirmation of email ownership before account activation. Each super administrator can have one verification record at a time, linked by foreign key to economic_board_super_administrators. This table is used during the registration flow to validate email ownership before granting superAdministrator privileges. Once the verification token is used, the used flag is set to true and the record is retained for audit purposes. This is a critical security mechanism that prevents unauthorized account creation and ensures all superAdministrators have valid, verified email addresses before being granted elevated privileges. {@link economic_board_super_administrators}.

Note: This table follows the same pattern as economic_board_citizen_email_verifications, economic_board_administrator_email_verifications, and other actor-specific verification tables, ensuring consistency across the authorization component.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the superAdministrator account that this verification record belongs to. {@link economic_board_super_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure random token used for verifying email ownership during registration. Must be a high-entropy, unpredictable string.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token expires and becomes invalid. All tokens have a limited lifetime for security.

plainFields.name: used
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether this verification token has been successfully used to verify the superAdministrator's email. Once set to true, the token cannot be reused.

models.name: economic_board_super_administrator_password_resets
models.description: Stores password reset tokens for superAdministrators with expiration timestamps to enable secure password recovery workflows. Each record represents a single password reset attempt tied to one superAdministrator. Tokens are single-use and expire after a set period. When a token is used, the record is marked as deleted. This table is purely operational and contains no business data beyond authentication state.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: References the superAdministrator who requested the password reset. {@link economic_board_super_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique, random token string used to authenticate the password reset request. Must be cryptographically secure and single-use.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the reset token expires. After this time, the token is invalid and cannot be used.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this password reset request was created.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When the token is used or expired and purged, this field is set to record deletion.

models.name: economic_board_profiles
models.description: Stores user display name and bio text for profile presentation in the economic_board platform. Contains fields for user-specific identity information that is separate from authentication credentials. Associated with user accounts via foreign key reference to the Authorization Agent's actor tables. This is a subsidiary table that is always managed through the citizen actor entity, as all user roles (administrator and superAdministrator) are promotions from the citizen role. The profile data belongs to the user's identity, not their role, and is referenced exclusively by economic_board_citizens.id.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen identity account that owns this profile. Since administrators and superAdministrators are promoted from citizens, all profiles are linked to economic_board_citizens.id and never to direct administrator or superAdministrator tables. This avoids multiple nullable foreign keys and maintains 3NF normalization.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: The public display name for the user profile. Must be non-empty and unique within the system. Used in article and comment attribution.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: A short biographical description provided by the user. Limited to 500 characters for layout consistency.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this profile was first created. Required for all business entities.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last profile update. Required for all business entities.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this profile was soft-deleted. Nullable to support soft-delete functionality. If null, profile is active.

models.name: economic_board_sections
models.description: Main section configuration with name, description, and status. Represents an organization category for articles on the discussion board (e.g., Politics, Economy). Each section serves as a thematic container for articles that are directly navigated and browsed by users, and managed exclusively by administrators through creation, editing, and deletion operations.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The unique name of the section that appears in the navigation UI. Must be unique across all sections.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the section's focus and purpose. Used in section listings and search indexing.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was logically deleted (soft-delete). Null means active.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the section. Values: 'active', 'deleted'. Used to control visibility without physical deletion.

models.name: economic_board_section_creations
models.description: Audit trail recording when a section was created, by which administrator, and which section was created. This immutable historical record tracks administrative actions on the section entity for compliance and debugging purposes. Each record represents a single section creation event linked to the administrator who performed it and the section that was created. {@link economic_board_sections.id} and {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: section_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the section that was created. {@link economic_board_sections.id}.

foreignFields.name: creator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator who created this section. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created.

models.name: economic_board_section_deletions
models.description: Audit trail that records every deletion event of a section on the economic_board platform. Each record contains the ID of the section that was deleted, the administrator who performed the deletion, and the precise timestamp of the deletion event. This table ensures transparency in administrative actions and enables forensic analysis of section lifecycle. References to the original section (economic_board_sections) and the administering administrator (economic_board_administrators) maintain referential integrity even after the section itself is removed from active records.

foreignFields.name: section_id
foreignFields.description: The section that was deleted. References the original section in economic_board_sections. {@link economic_board_sections.id}.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed the section deletion. References the administrator account in economic_board_administrators. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The precise timestamp when the section deletion was recorded. This is the audit timestamp indicating when the deletion event occurred.

models.name: economic_board_articles
models.description: Core article entity containing title, content, section reference, author reference, and publication metadata. Articles are the primary content units on the economic discussion board, created and managed by citizens. Each article is assigned to exactly one section and authored by exactly one citizen. This table is the foundation for all article-related operations including creation, editing, deletion, searching, and viewing. Foreign keys link to economic_board_citizens (author) and economic_board_sections (section). All temporal fields (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are included to support soft deletion, audit trails, and time-based queries. This table is designed for full-text search capability using GIN indexes on title and content.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen author of this article. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the section this article belongs to. {@link economic_board_sections.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title (required), limited to 200 characters. Used for search, display in lists, and metadata.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Full text content of the article (required), limited to 50,000 characters. This is the main body of the article content, where users express their economic or political analysis and arguments.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was first created. Immutable, used for sorting articles by publication date. Follows Asia/Seoul timezone.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the article's title or content. Updated on every edit within the allowed time window.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was logically deleted. Null if active. Used for soft deletion to preserve audit trails while hiding inactive content from users.

models.name: economic_board_article_files
models.description: Stores metadata for all non-image file attachments to articles, including original filename, size, MIME type, and storage path. This is a subsidiary entity that exists only in the context of an article and is managed through article creation/editing, not independently.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article to which this file is attached. {@link economic_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: uploaded_by_id
foreignFields.description: The user who uploaded this file. {@link economic_board_citizens.id} or {@link economic_board_administrators.id} or {@link economic_board_super_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: The original filename as provided by the user during upload.

plainFields.name: size_bytes
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., application/pdf, text/plain).

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: The secure storage path where the file is stored (e.g., /files/uuid-filename.pdf).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this file's metadata.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was logically deleted (null if active).

models.name: economic_board_article_images
models.description: Store metadata for all image attachments to articles, including original filename, dimensions, thumbnail paths, and storage locations. Each image is associated with exactly one article (many images per article). This table stores the physical and metadata attributes of uploaded images, including original dimensions and optimized versions for display. Images are never accessed directly by users but are embedded within article content, making this a subsidiary entity managed solely through its parent article.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article this image is attached to. {@link economic_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: The original filename provided by the user when uploading the image.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: The width of the original image in pixels.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: The height of the original image in pixels.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: The MIME type of the image (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png) to ensure correct rendering.

plainFields.name: original_path
plainFields.description: The storage path where the original, full-resolution image is stored.

plainFields.name: thumbnail_path
plainFields.description: The storage path where the thumbnail (300x300px) version of this image is stored.

plainFields.name: medium_path
plainFields.description: The storage path where the medium-sized (1200x1200px) version of this image is stored for viewing in article detail.

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the image was uploaded and stored.

plainFields.name: economic_board_citizen_id
plainFields.description: Reference to the citizen who uploaded this image. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

models.name: economic_board_article_view_stats
models.description:
Aggregated view statistics for articles, tracking total views and unique viewers per article.

This table provides performance metrics for article engagement without storing individual view events, which would be inefficient at scale. All values are aggregate counters updated on each view, with atomic increments to handle concurrent traffic.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article this view statistics belongs to. {@link economic_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: total_views
plainFields.description: Total number of times this article has been viewed by any user, including multiple views by the same user.

plainFields.name: unique_viewers
plainFields.description: Number of unique users who have viewed this article at least once.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this view statistics record was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this view statistics record was last updated.

models.name: economic_board_comments
models.description: Stores user comments on articles with content, timestamps, and relationships to users and articles. Each comment has a single parent article and is authored by one user. Comments include text content, creation timestamp, last edited timestamp, and deletion status. This single table handles all comment operations as specified: creation, editing (within 1-hour window), deletion, and reading. Foreign keys link to economic_board_users (author) and economic_board_articles (parent article). Comments are displayed sorted by oldest first and are paginated. The table supports moderation workflows with soft deletion and administrative deletion tracking. All comment metadata is stored in raw form without calculated fields to maintain 3NF compliance.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_articles_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article this comment belongs to. {@link economic_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: economic_board_users_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user who authored this comment. {@link economic_board_citizens.id} or {@link economic_board_administrators.id} or {@link economic_board_super_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The text content of the comment, limited to 2,500 characters as per business rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was originally created. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last edited. Updated only when author modifies content within the 1-hour edit window.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was marked as deleted. Null if comment is active. Supports soft delete for audit trails.

plainFields.name: deleted_by_admin
plainFields.description: Flag that indicates if the comment was deleted by an administrator (true) or by the author (false). Maintains audit trail of deletion actions.

plainFields.name: deletion_reason
plainFields.description: Optional reason provided by an administrator when deleting a comment. Stored only when deleted_by_admin is true.

models.name: economic_board_bans
models.description: Records each user ban event with reason, administrator who issued the ban, and timestamp. This table logs when a citizen has been banned from the platform by an administrator, including the reason for the ban and timestamps for when the ban was issued and (if applicable) lifted. The ban status of a user is determined by the existence of an active (unbanned_at is null) record in this table. The system tracks which administrator imposed each ban for accountability and audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_citizens_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen account that has been banned. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_administrators_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who issued this ban. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the administrator for imposing the ban. Must be at least 10 characters according to requirements. This text will be displayed to administrators viewing the banned users list.

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the ban was issued. This is required for all ban records to establish when the restriction began.

plainFields.name: unbanned_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the ban was lifted, if applicable. If null, the ban is still active. This allows tracking of both temporary and permanent bans, and supports the unban functionality.

models.name: economic_board_file_attachments
models.description: Primary table storing metadata for file attachments uploaded to articles, including filename, size, MIME type, upload timestamp, and a foreign key to an actor's unique identifier. This is the central entity that enforces the polymorphic ownership pattern through 1NF decomposition. Each file attachment has exactly one owner, but that owner type can be a citizen, administrator, or superAdministrator, each with their own subsidiary table for type-safe references.

foreignFields.name: actor_identifier
foreignFields.description: Unique identifier of the actor who uploaded this file. This is a polymorphic reference that can point to any actor in the system, with the actual actor type determined by which subsidiary table contains the matching record. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}, {@link economic_board_administrators.id}, or {@link economic_board_super_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: The original name of the uploaded file as provided by the user. This field is used for display and search purposes. Must be preserved exactly as provided for compliance with file identification.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: The size of the uploaded file in bytes. Required to enforce upload quotas and display file size information.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: The MIME type of the file determined during upload validation. This ensures security by verifying the file type before allowing storage and download.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the file was uploaded. This field is required for audit trails and temporal sorting of uploads.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the file metadata was last updated. This field is required for consistency tracking and allows the system to detect recent modifications.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this file attachment was logically deleted. May be null if file is still active. Used for soft deletion to preserve audit history without losing file metadata.

models.name: economic_board_image_attachments
models.description:
Stores metadata for image attachments uploaded to articles, including original filename, size, dimensions, MIME type, upload timestamp, uploader ID, and paths to original and optimized thumbnail/medium versions.

This is a purely subsidiary entity - image attachments cannot exist independently from their parent article. They are always created, updated, and deleted through article operations.

All metadata is stored with maximum fidelity to support responsive image delivery, file integrity checking, and audit trails. Original filenames are preserved for user reference while unique storage paths ensure security and avoid conflicts. Thumbnail and medium versions are optimized for performance while maintaining the original for archival purposes.

Referenced by economic_board_articles via one-to-many relationship: each article can have multiple image attachments, but each image belongs to exactly one article.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: References the parent article that this image is attached to. {@link economic_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: The original filename as provided by the user during upload. Preserved for user reference and metadata purposes.

plainFields.name: size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes. Used for storage quota calculations and download progress tracking.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Image width in pixels. Used for responsive display and layout calculations.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Image height in pixels. Used for responsive display and layout calculations.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the image (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png). Used for content-type headers during delivery and validation.

plainFields.name: upload_timestamp
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image was uploaded. Matches the article creation timestamp context when possible.

plainFields.name: uploader_id
plainFields.description: The UUID of the user who uploaded this image. References economic_board_citizens, economic_board_administrators, or economic_board_super_administrators via polymorphic relation handled at application layer.

plainFields.name: original_path
plainFields.description: Storage path to the original, unmodified image file. Used for direct downloads and archival access.

plainFields.name: thumbnail_path
plainFields.description: Storage path to the 300x300 pixel thumbnail version. Used for efficient display in article lists and previews.

plainFields.name: medium_path
plainFields.description: Storage path to the 1200x1200 pixel optimized version. Used for detailed view in article content pages.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Standard temporal field - record creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Standard temporal field - record last update time.

models.name: economic_board_file_attachment_of_citizens
models.description: Subsidiary table for file attachments uploaded by citizens. Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship with a primary file_attachment record, ensuring only citizens can upload files through this path. This table enforces access control by restricting file uploads to citizen users while using the generic economic_board_file_attachments as the core storage mechanism.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_file_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: The unique file attachment record this citizen is associated with. {@link economic_board_file_attachments.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this association was created. Standard temporal field for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this association was last updated. Standard temporal field for audit trail.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this association was logically deleted. Standard soft-delete field for audit trail.

models.name: economic_board_file_attachment_of_administrators
models.description: Subsidiary table for file attachments uploaded by administrators. Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship with a primary file_attachment record, ensuring only administrators can upload files through this path.

foreignFields.name: file_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Primary file attachment record this subsidiary record belongs to. {@link economic_board_file_attachments.id}

models.name: economic_board_file_attachment_ofs
models.description: Subsidiary table for file attachments uploaded by superAdministrators. Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship with a primary file_attachment record, ensuring only superAdministrators can upload files through this path. This enables role-based upload authorization without duplicating metadata.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_file_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: References the primary file attachment record. This enforces a 1:1 relationship where each superAdministrator upload corresponds to exactly one file_attachment.

models.name: economic_board_search_indices
models.description: Full-text search index mapping article IDs to searchable text fields (title and content). This table enables fast keyword matching on article titles and content without scanning original article data. Each entry represents one searchable text unit associated with an article. Maintains referential integrity with articles table and provides optimized full-text search capabilities through GIN indexing.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the associated article in the economic_board_articles table. {@link economic_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: searchable_text
plainFields.description: Combined text content of the article title and body content for full-text search capabilities. This field is indexed with a GIN index to enable efficient fuzzy matching and text search operations

models.name: economic_board_search_tags
models.description: Normalized, de-duplicated list of all tags used across articles. Each tag is stored once with a unique ID, enabling efficient filtering and reducing data redundancy. Tag text is stored in lowercase after trimming whitespace to ensure case-insensitive matching. This table serves as the canonical source for filtering articles by tag. No other component should maintain a duplicate tag list.

plainFields.name: text
plainFields.description: The normalized tag text. Stored in lowercase after trimming whitespace to ensure case-insensitive matches during filtering. Maximum 50 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tag was first created and inserted into the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tag was last updated (if ever modified).

models.name: economic_board_search_article_tags
models.description: Junction table defining the many-to-many relationship between articles and tags. Each row represents an association between one article and one tag, allowing filtering of articles by any combination of tags using AND logic. This table eliminates data redundancy and enables efficient search filtering while maintaining third normal form.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: References the article being tagged. {@link economic_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: tag_id
foreignFields.description: References the tag associated with the article. {@link economic_board_search_tags.id}.

models.name: economic_board_search_results
models.description: Cache table storing search query parameters and result metadata for pagination and sorting. Each record represents one unique search query with its parameters (keywords, sort direction, tags), result count, and pagination metadata to avoid repeated query execution on identical requests. This table enables fast retrieval of previously executed searches by storing the combination of search criteria and results, improving response times for repetitive queries on the same search parameters.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to article that this search result is associated with. This allows counting articles matching the search criteria. {@link economic_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: search_terms
plainFields.description: Full text search terms entered by the user. Stores the complete search query string for matching against future requests. Must be non-null as every search must have terms.

plainFields.name: sort_direction
plainFields.description: Sorting direction for the search results. Must be either 'newest' or 'oldest' as specified in search requirements. This value determines whether results are ordered by creation date descending or ascending.

plainFields.name: page
plainFields.description: Page number of the search results being cached. Represents the current page of results (1-based indexing) as specified in the pagination requirements.

plainFields.name: per_page
plainFields.description: Number of results per page. Specifies how many articles are displayed per page in the pagination system, typically 20 as required.

plainFields.name: result_count
plainFields.description: Total number of articles matching this search query. Represents the total count of results across all pages for this specific search criteria.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this search result cache entry was created. Used for cache expiration and analytics. Follows standard temporal field pattern and uses server time (Asia/Seoul).

plainFields.name: tag_filters
plainFields.description: JSON-encoded array of tag names used for filtering search results. Stores multiple tags in string format to enable efficient tag-based filtering without requiring junction table joins.

models.name: economic_board_admin_requests
models.description: Records administrator promotion requests submitted by citizens, including the reason text, submission timestamp, and status. Each request is initiated by a citizen and processed by a super administrator. This is a primary entity in the administrative workflow, requiring independent access, filtering by status, search on reason text, and audit trails of approval/rejection actions.

foreignFields.name: requester_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen who submitted the administrator request. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: processed_by_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator who processed this request. {@link economic_board_super_administrators.id}. Nullable until request is processed.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the administrator request. Must be one of: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: reason_text
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the citizen for seeking administrator promotion. Must be between 50 and 1000 characters, trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the request was submitted by the citizen. Always required and immutable.

plainFields.name: processed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the request was processed (approved or rejected) by a super administrator. Null until processing occurs.
